entries.test: Global project construction records and financing terms would establish capacity under construction versus announced capacity and how many associated loans require only interest payments.
entries.note: The loan-payment inference requires evidence beyond construction totals.

entries.test: Subscription disclosures and usage records for the cases he identifies would show token visibility and whether token costs exceed subscription prices.
entries.note: The universal assertion is restricted to cases he has found. Token retail prices and providers' actual costs must be distinguished.

entries.test: Published financial and customer-growth records would show whether below-cost subscriptions drove rapid growth while leaving the products dependent on continuing outside funding.
entries.note: 'Infinite resources' has a plain contextual reading of indefinitely subsidized losses.

entries.test: Comparable coding-task measurements, token pricing histories, and disclosed serving costs would show whether additional reasoning tokens increased total costs despite lower token prices.
entries.note: Calling the reductions a marketing move adds an attribution of purpose beyond the measurable cost relationship.

entries.test: Cursor's funding announcements and cumulative revenue through publication would establish whether it raised $3.36 billion while earning at most approximately $1 billion.
entries.note: The central revenue ceiling is firm; the aside about fluctuating months does not make it merely probabilistic.

entries.test: Startup financial disclosures and closures, together with the labs' API revenue disclosures, would show whether model costs make these startups unsustainable and eliminate the associated revenue.
entries.note: This is a sweeping, undated prediction, not merely a warning of possible failures.

entries.test: Compute contracts, utilization disclosures, and financial reports would show whether both companies hold unnecessary reservations they cannot afford because growth missed their projections.

entries.note: The combined claim uses unbounded historical superlatives and a violent exaggeration rather than a shared factual standard.
Neither the scope nor observable consequence of 'break the illusion' is specified. A failed exit alone would not establish what counts as fulfillment.

entries.test: AI companies' financial reports, model dependencies, and intellectual-property records would establish whether every company loses money on inference and lacks intellectual property because of those dependencies.
entries.note: 'Problem child' is evaluative, but the universal financial and intellectual-property assertions are testable.

entries.test: Historical AWS investment and profitability records, Uber growth and losses, and corresponding AI-company financial records would allow comparison of their buildout costs and business economics.
entries.note: The surrounding discussion supplies the financial dimensions of the comparison.

entries.test: AI labs' financial statements and accounting policies would show whether model training is a recurring operating expense rather than capital expenditure.
entries.note: The passage also contains an undated prediction that training costs will persist.

entries.test: Anthropic's promotion dates, peak-hour policy disclosures, and reproducible usage measurements would show whether the overlapping changes made subscribers' available access less ascertainable.
entries.note: The extracted proposition appropriately excludes the separate 'might be' judgment about a swindle.

entries.test: Subsequent pricing, usage-limit, and cost-cutting announcements from both companies before their S-1 filings would establish whether several major tightening measures followed.
entries.note: 'I wager' functions here as an affirmative prediction. No calendar deadline is supplied.
The composite characterization of the companies as inherently abusive is a moral judgment; specific alleged acts could be assessed separately.
The central claim concerns adoption in an unrealized historical pricing scenario. The productivity assertion is separately testable.
'I don't really see how' expresses doubt about a solution rather than committing to its impossibility.

entries.test: Industry revenue estimates, service costs, and observed demand at sustainable prices would test the $65 billion figure and whether all demand depends on subsidies.
entries.note: Evidence of sustained demand for unsubsidized AI services could refute the universal claim. The prospective pricing condition is not an inaccessible historical counterfactual.

entries.test: Demonstrated large-scale customer adoption at sustainable prices or a commercially deployed breakthrough that materially reduces serving costs would refute the claim.
entries.note: Context gives 'pricing that makes sense' the concrete meaning of economically sustainable pricing.
'Mandate of Heaven' is a mocking metaphor for industry entitlement, not a literal belief claim.

entries.test: Big-tech capex disclosures, NVIDIA revenue and customer data, and subsequent AI investment trends would show whether capex reductions signal a broader contraction and whether those purchases exclusively drive NVIDIA's growth.
entries.note: The claim combines a conditional warning with a presently testable assertion about NVIDIA's growth sources.
The warning specifies no agreed consequence of an IPO delay. The accounting remark and disaster analogy supply no definite financial test.

entries.test: SoftBank's debt maturities, loan-to-asset calculations, liquid assets, and financing terms would show whether the borrowing materially increases near-term repayment or refinancing risk.
entries.note: The preceding sentences give 'precarious' a concrete financial meaning and supply the proposition's antecedent.

entries.test: If ARM trades below $80, SoftBank's ARM-backed loan terms, collateral requirements, and financing disclosures would show whether that price creates material financial pressure.
entries.note: The immediately preceding discussion of a $15 billion margin loan supplies a financial reading of 'hairy.'
